alternatives.name: cosign
alternatives.why_not_default: cosign signs and verifies artifacts and software identity. It does not version data observations, their lineage or their availability. Its card says no signing or identity flow was initiated and that some upstreams publish only checksums (packet lines 6-10). The only evidence is an external README at v3.1.3, which I did not open. Use it only if there is a demonstrated need to sign retained receipt or ledger manifests beyond the existing external SHA-256 anchors.

alternatives.name: data-kafka
alternatives.why_not_default: Kafka is a replay log for multiple independent consumers. The retained ledger comes from one bounded acquisition, and no multi-consumer streaming need has been shown. The card says single-node synthetic replay is only a prospective smoke check, ordering is per partition, and transactions do not make external sinks exactly-once (packet lines 71-73). The upstream metadata is incomplete: latest is 'show' and released_at is null (lines 91 and 95). The evidence is an unopened external README.

alternatives.name: foundation-socraticode
alternatives.why_not_default: Its native evidence is real, but it covers the code-retrieval layer, not market-data provenance. evidence/receipts/native-rag.json records native Codex and Claude codebase_search returning tools/ecosystem/linux-usage-report.cjs lines 2-39 (score 0.6429), an index of 35 files and 139 chunks, and add/update/delete watch phases. That touches only the 'index-freshness' scope term. It does not preserve feed, timestamp, security identity or corporate-action provenance, and it does not produce analytical snapshots. The card also notes AGPL-3.0 obligations (packet line 103).

alternatives.name: data-openlineage
alternatives.why_not_default: OpenLineage is a lineage event standard. Its card says it is not a persistent lineage server or dataset version store (packet line 138), so it cannot produce exact snapshots. The architecture table allows 'SQLMesh/OpenLineage/Marquez only for demonstrated transformation/lineage needs. Neither format nor lineage alone proves time correctness.' (blueprints/us-equities/architecture/README.md line 49). No such need has been demonstrated, and the upstream README is unopened.

alternatives.name: data-arcticdb
alternatives.why_not_default: ArcticDB is a versioned dataframe store, but its licence is unresolved. The card says the current release is BSL-1.1 source-available, and vendor prose about paid production or business use conflicts with the pinned Additional Use Grant (packet lines 169-170). The upstream licence is NOASSERTION (line 190). The card also warns that storage version time is not proof of market information availability (line 171). Nothing was executed and the README is unopened.

alternatives.name: data-mlflow
alternatives.why_not_default: MLflow tracks experiment runs, metrics and artifacts. That is model lineage, not lineage of source observations, and it overlaps with DVC's experiment pipelines. The card says 'No experiments or models were run by this review' and that autologging does not capture every data revision or leakage decision (packet lines 201-202). The README is unopened.

alternatives.name: data-iceberg
alternatives.why_not_default: Iceberg's open table snapshots fit the 'snapshot-store' term. However, the card says catalog creation alone would not prove append, multi-writer conflict handling, cross-engine compatibility or time travel. It also says snapshot expiry can destroy required audit versions and that storage snapshots do not imply past information availability (packet lines 232-233). No local measurement shows that the single-process DuckDB/Parquet ledger needs a table format. The README is unopened.

arms: project-native DuckDB/Parquet ledger with SHA-256 manifest anchors (baseline)
c6 ArcticDB versioned library (after licence resolution)
overturn_protocol.metric: Byte-exact reproduction of an anchored eligible selection (count plus SHA-256) at a pinned version after the source is modified and restored. Rows with unknown availability must still be rejected. For each arm, also report the added operational steps and dependency footprint, and whether it adds anything beyond the existing SHA-256 manifest anchors.

overturn_when: Run a comparison on the security-identity ledger. First establish a baseline with "$SDK_PYTHON" -m unittest tests.test_security_identity -v and the ledger.py materialize/select commands (blueprints/us-equities/security-identity/README.md lines 76-81). Then version the same materialized ledger (Parquet, manifest, select.sql) with DVC (c2), Apache Iceberg/PyIceberg (c8) and ArcticDB (c6, once its licence is resolved). For each arm, check whether it reproduces a byte-identical anchored eligible selection at a pinned revision after the source is modified and restored, while still rejecting rows with unknown availability or validity. The verdict changes in either of two cases: (a) c8 or c6 passes where c2 fails, or (b) c2 adds no reproducibility or branch-lock capability beyond the existing SHA-256 manifest anchors. In case (b), the layer default reverts to the project-native ledger, and DVC is kept only as a conditional option for branched datasets.
why_selected: c2 (DVC) is a conditional default chosen by source-review fit only. No adopted candidate was executed, measured or integrated for this layer in any evidence I opened. I observed three things. (1) The packet card (packet lines 36-66) describes DVC as 'Git-linked hashes, data dependencies and experiment pipelines', pinned at 3.67.1 / source 356dfa03, Apache-2.0. Its limitation reads 'Content hashes prove identity, not data validity or point-in-time correctness' (line 39). Among the adopted candidates, only this role maps directly onto the data-versioning, provenance and reproducibility scope terms (packet lines 284-297) without a new server, table format or licence question. (2) The repository keeps an independent upstream source inspection of DVC. catalogs/us-equities/data-evaluation-followup.md line 46 cites treeverse/dvc at 56e59829 (dvc/stage/serialize.py and commands/repro.py) for 'data/parameter lock provenance when datasets branch'. That is a different revision from the packet pin 356dfa03, and the same line limits the value: 'Current receipts already cover the small workflow; hashes and dry runs do not prove PIT or data rights.' (3) The working provenance mechanism in this repository uses none of the candidates. It is the project's own DuckDB/Parquet ledger. Its manifest binds exact source, Parquet, bridge, helper and SQL bytes under external SHA-256 anchors (blueprints/us-equities/security-identity/README.md lines 138-144), with separate event, observed and available nanosecond axes. Historical validity and publication fields stay Unknown (lines 107-116) or NULL (lines 41-42 and 194-195). That ledger is documented design with synthetic offline tests, and I did not run it. DVC is therefore selected only as the lightest adopted way to version and lock those ledger artifacts once datasets branch. Its added value over the existing SHA-256 anchors has not been demonstrated, and the availability-cutoff and eligibility rejection logic stays in project code. I did not use the withheld review_status label (packet line 326) as a basis for selection.
